mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month preceding the prediction is associated with a short-term discounting effect that reduces expected future cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and inflation is stable.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (labor market employment) of at least 2% coinciding with a decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) suggests strengthening labor demand, which is associated with higher equity valuations and positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly increase ≥ 2% and UNRATE monthly decrease
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when the labor demand/unsaturation signal is present but SPX underperforms.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in GDPC1 (real private consumption) of 3% or more over the prior two months predicts increased future economic activity, which elevates equity valuations and drives positive 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when GDPC1 growth is as specified but broader macro conditions are adverse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in INDPRO (industrial production index) below 100 over two consecutive months signals supply-side weakness, which is expected to depress corporate earnings and produce negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during INDPRO contractions when other demand indicators are neutral.

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL (CPI) rises by more than 0.5% in a single month and FEDFUNDS remains below 2%, it indicates persistent inflation pressure without strong policy response, which is associated with negative 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when the inflation signal is present but the market underreacts.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in UNRATE below 4.5% for three consecutive months in a labor market recovery regime is expected to boost investor confidence and drive positive 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the low-unemployment regime when other risk factors are neutral.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly rise in HOUST (housing starts) and PAYEMS (labor) exceeding 5% and 3%, respectively, signals robust dual demand, which is expected to support equity valuations and produce positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly increase > 5% and PAYEMS monthly increase > 3%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) when both signals are present but broader macro uncertainty is high.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged monthly decline in RSAFS (retail sales) of 4% or more indicates weakening consumer demand, which is expected to lower corporate earnings and drive negative 20-day forward returns regardless of monetary policy stance.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during RSAFS declines when other demand indicators are stable.
